en.title: Hurricane Ridge snow forecast: 5–24 in expected by 25 November (US West)
en.description: At Hurricane Ridge the freezing level reaches 5,446 ft (1,660 m) to 6,594 ft (2,010 m) on 24 November, higher than the top (5,446 ft / 1,660 m): rain …
en.lede: At Hurricane Ridge the freezing level reaches 5,446 ft (1,660 m) to 6,594 ft (2,010 m) on 24 November, higher than the top (5,446 ft / 1,660 m): rain or wet snow is possible on all slopes, and some of the snow may turn to runoff. Mixed rain and snow: snow is expected only up high, about 5–24 in (61 cm) near the top of Hurricane Ridge (5,446 ft (1,660 m)), with rain below about 4,528 ft (1,380 m). By 25 November the forecast adds 5–24 in (61 cm) at Hurricane Ridge, 6–15 in (38 cm) at Mt Baker and 9 in (22 cm) at Stevens Pass to the snowpack. Two kinds of numbers here: model estimates for the upper slopes of each resort, and station measurements that are exact but cover one point on the date shown. Snow in the mountains is water held back for spring: what falls now feeds rivers and reservoirs later.

p: The deepest snowpack of this group is at Mt. Shasta Ski Park, about 24 in (61 cm) on the upper slopes; next are Hurricane Ridge 10 in (25 cm) and Stevens Pass 9 in (23 cm).
Today 434,145 sq mi (1,124,430 km²) of ground in the US West is covered by snow, our model says, and 186 of 193 resorts have snow on their upper slopes.
At about 5,157 ft (1,572 m), Hurricane Ridge has 4 in (11 cm) today; a normal 22 November has 10 in (26 cm) there.
That is more than in 14 of the 46 past winters on this date.
In past winters the best snow at Hurricane Ridge usually came early March / early April.
A slow start is common and says little about January; for now the highest lifts and the runs with snowmaking are the safe choice.
Day by day at Hurricane Ridge: Sunday 22 November 2 in (4 cm); Monday 23 November 6 in (16 cm); Tuesday 24 November 11 in (29 cm); Wednesday 25 November 6 in (16 cm).

Height by height at Hurricane Ridge: 4,872 ft (1,485 m) 6 in (15 cm) on the ground, 14 in (36 cm) more in the next 7 days; 5,157 ft (1,572 m) 6 in (16 cm) on the ground, 18 in (46 cm) more in the next 7 days; 5,446 ft (1,660 m) 7 in (18 cm) on the ground, 22 in (56 cm) more in the next 7 days.

sections.h: The next days in the forecast
p: More snow, and so more stored water, is on the way: by 25 November our forecast gives 7 in (18 cm) at Alpental and 7 in (17 cm) at Mt. Shasta Ski Park.

The snow-covered area has grown from 406,318 sq mi (1,052,360 km²) on 20 November to 434,145 sq mi (1,124,430 km²) today, and our forecast gives 357,890 sq mi (926,930 km²) on 25 November: more ground is storing water as snow.

sections.h: Where snow stays, where it melts
p: On 24 November the freezing level at Mt Baker rises to 2,822 ft (860 m) to 6,398 ft (1,950 m), above the top of the resort (5,105 ft / 1,556 m): precipitation can fall as rain or wet snow, and rain on snow speeds up the melt.

Height changes everything at Hurricane Ridge: our model gives 6 in (15 cm) at the base (4,872 ft / 1,485 m), 6 in (16 cm) at mid-mountain (5,157 ft / 1,572 m) and 7 in (18 cm) at the top (5,446 ft / 1,660 m).
Forecasts a few days ahead can change: look at the map again the day before you travel.

advice: Forecasts a few days ahead can change: look at the map again the day before you travel.
When the freezing level rises above the resort, part of the snow melts as it falls: expect wet snow and stay near the top.
Be on the first lift after a snowfall: by midday, sun and skiers have already changed the snow.
Before you ski off-piste or go touring, read the official avalanche bulletin (links below).
